item.title: Accurate ab initio calculations of the ground state properties of singly charged alkali metal hydrides
item.description: arXiv:2610.31161v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this article, we investigate the ground state electronic properties of singly charged alkali metal hydrides using the single-reference coupled-cluster method with single and double excitations (CCSD), together with perturbative triple excitations (CCSD(T)). A large relativistic core-valence quintuple-zeta basis set has been employed. The calculated spectroscopic constants and molecular properties are compared with existing data in the literature. Further, the relevant vibrational parameters are determined by solving the vibrational Schr\"odinger equation utilizing potential energy curves and permanent dipole moment curves. Thereafter, spontaneous and black-body radiation induced transition rates are calculated to obtain the lifetimes of the vibrational states.
item.dc:creator: Ankush Thakur, Renu Bala, H. S. Nataraj

item.title: Fock-space relativistic coupled-cluster study of systematic shifts and fine-structure constant sensitivity in {\rm Cf$^{17+}$}, {\rm Cm$^{15+}$} and {\rm Bk$^{16+}$} highly charged ions
item.description: arXiv:2610.31231v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Highly charged ions (HCIs) are among the most promising candidates proposed for the development of next-generation optical clocks and the precision tests of fundamental physics. In this work, we investigate the clock-relevant properties of $\rm Cf^{17+}$, $\rm Cm^{15+}$ and $\rm Bk^{16+}$ HCIs using Fock-space relativistic coupled-cluster (FSRCC) theory. The corrections from Breit interaction, QED effects and perturbative triples are incorporated to improve the accuracy of results further. We compute excitation energies, transition amplitudes, lifetimes, hyperfine structure constants, electric quadrupole moments, and electric dipole polarizabilities for low-lying states of these ions. These properties are further used to characterize important clock transitions and estimate key systematic frequency shifts. Our calculations reveal that the proposed clock transitions exhibit strongly suppressed systematic frequency shifts. We also compute the sensitivity coefficients, $q$, and enhancement factors, $K_{\alpha}$, for the proposed clock transition as a probe to variation in the fine-structure constant, $\alpha$. Our calculations predict exceptionally large $K_{\alpha}$ of $-55.3$ and $57.5$ for $5f_{5/2} \rightarrow 6p_{1/2}$ transition in $\rm Cf^{17+}$ and $6p_{1/2} \rightarrow 5f_{5/2}$ transition in $\rm Bk^{16+}$, respectively. These giant $K_{\alpha}$s place the proposed transitions among the most sensitive optical probes for the laboratory searches for $\alpha$ variation. Further, a comparative analysis of proposed transitions in $\rm Cm^{15+}$ and $\rm Bk^{16+}$ shows that, $5f_{5/2} \rightarrow 5f_{7/2}$ transition possess smaller systematic shifts and is therefore attractive for precision frequency metrology, whereas $6p_{1/2} \rightarrow 5f_{5/2}$ transition exhibit significantly enhanced sensitivity to $\alpha$ variation.
item.dc:creator: Palki Gakkhar, D. Angom, B. K. Mani

item.title: Lifetime of the singly charged $^{229}$Th nuclear isomer
item.description: arXiv:2610.31009v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The nucleus of thorium-229 ($^{229}$Th) has an exceptionally low-energy isomeric state ($^{229\mathrm{m}}$Th). Because its excitation energy is close to the energy levels of valence electrons, the lifetime of $^{229\mathrm{m}}$Th varies substantially depending on its electronic state. Although internal conversion and radiative decay were recently observed, the electronic bridge decay of $^{229\mathrm{m}}$Th, a higher-order decay process through an electronic transition, has not yet been confirmed. A promising candidate to search for this decay channel is singly charged $^{229\mathrm{m}}$Th$^+$ in the electronic ground state. Here we produce $^{229\mathrm{m}}$Th$^+$ by a charge exchange reaction in an ion trap and detect the isomers through measuring the electrons emitted from internal conversion processes. We determined the half-life of $^{229\mathrm{m}}$Th$^+$ to be 0.46(8) s. Our result differs by several orders of magnitude from the half-lives of internal conversion and radiative decay, indirectly suggesting the existence of the electronic bridge decay of $^{229\mathrm{m}}$Th. This will enable the direct observation and further investigation of the electronic bridge process, which will contribute to understanding nuclear-electron interactions and accelerating nuclear deexcitation in the operation of a thorium-based nuclear clock.
item.dc:creator: Y. Shigekawa, A. Yamaguchi, K. Tokoi, N. Sato, H. Kikunaga, K. Shirasaki, Y. Kasamatsu, M. Wada, H. Haba

item.title: Realization of a Superleak in a Quantum Gas
item.description: arXiv:2610.31185v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Ultracold quantum gases offer a controllable and microscopically accessible platform for understanding and engineering superfluidity. Yet, realizing a superleak that selectively transports the superfluid while suppressing normal flow has remained elusive. Here, we harness an optical superlattice to realize such a superleak through dynamical selectivity. The superfluid undergoes coherent Josephson transport, whereas the normal component exhibits slow, thermodynamically limited response, resulting in a flow-rate contrast of 500(49). Exploiting this contrast, we demonstrate repeated filtering of the normal component and dynamical purification of the superfluid, while sustaining coherent driven oscillations for up to 100 cycles. Our results establish a controllable atomic superleak and open possibilities for manipulating transport and thermodynamics in quantum fluids.
item.dc:creator: Wan-Ling Yang, Shao-Bo Liu, Xiang Luo, Chao Yang, Hai-Lin Li, Yu-Zhou Yang, Yong-Kui Wang, Bing Yang

item.title: Predictive electronic feedback control for narrow-linewidth lasers
item.description: arXiv:2610.31396v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Narrow-linewidth lasers are essential for various key atom-laser interaction processes and optical setups in quantum coherent control, quantum precision measurement, and quantum information science. The Pound-Drever-Hall (PDH) technique is the standard method for the frequency-stabilization of narrow-linewidth lasers, but the inherent time delay in its feedback loop inevitably induces excessive phase noise, commonly known as servo bumps. Previous solutions primarily rely on additional optical components outside the electronic feedback control loop. Here, we propose and implement a generic method based on the Smith predictor to address the time-delay issue entirely within the electronic part of the PDH feedback control loop. We systematically demonstrate its capability to suppress phase noise and reduce servo bumps by adding only a single Field-Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) controller to the loop. This class of methods is demonstrated to be conceptually concise with minimal hardware overhead, effective in practice, and holds potential for a wide variety of future applications.
item.dc:creator: Jiatian Liu, Xuan Qi, Xiayang Fan, Shenchao Jin, Yuan Sun

item.title: Macroscopic Nuclear Resonance Energy Transfer Mediated by Coherent Magnons
item.description: arXiv:2610.31507v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Phonon-mediated nuclear Resonance Energy Transfer (RET) in metal deuterides is severely constrained by inertial rest-mass dilution, lattice fracture limits, and thermal nuclear spin cancellation. Extending the generalized nuclear Dicke model to Ferromagnetic Resonance (FMR) magnons eliminates mass dilution via hyperfine-amplified M1 coupling while unlocking relativistic Dirac M2 coupling via Overhauser spin polarization. We derive a Suhl-clamped FMR scaling law predicting 14.2 MeV (Pd-106) and 11.4 MeV (Ni-58) breakup neutrons, 19.9 MeV alpha particles, and reconciled sub-keV fusion anomalies.
item.dc:creator: Ryan Weed

item.title: In-Situ Differential-Light-Shift Cancellation for Trapped-Atom Clocks
item.description: arXiv:2603.26398v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Differential light shifts (DLS) induced by optical trapping fields fundamentally limit the stability and accuracy of trapped-atom microwave clocks. We demonstrate an in-situ method to cancel DLS by simultaneously interrogating multiple spatially separated atomic ensembles at different trap intensities generated from a common light source. By operating the ensembles at set intensity ratios and performing Ramsey spectroscopy, the intensity-dependent frequency shifts are measured within each experimental cycle and extrapolated to the zero-intensity limit. This approach effectively enables shot-to-shot determination of a DLS-free frequency without requiring magic wavelengths or species-specific cancellation schemes. We validate the method for Rb atoms trapped in time-averaged potentials by introducing controlled variations of the total trap power and show that the extrapolated frequency remains insensitive to these fluctuations. The technique is general and can be extended to other systematic shifts, providing a scalable route toward improved stability and accuracy in compact trapped-atom clocks and related quantum sensors relying on optical dipole traps
item.dc:creator: Jan Simon Haase, Alexander Fieguth, Igor Br\"ockel, Jens Kruse, Carsten Klempt

item.title: Quantum theory of molecular orientation
item.description: arXiv:2403.04572v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We formulate a quantum phase space for rotational and nuclear-spin states of rigid molecules. For each nuclear spin isomer, we re-derive the isomer's admissible angular momentum states from molecular geometry and nuclear-spin data, introduce its angular position states using quantization theory, and develop a generalized Fourier transform converting between the two. We classify molecules into three types -- asymmetric, rotationally symmetric, and perrotationally symmetric -- with the last type having no macroscopic analogue due to nuclear-spin statistics constraints. We discuss two general features in perrotationally symmetric state spaces that are Hamiltonian-independent and induced solely by symmetry and spin statistics. First, we quantify when and how an isomer's state space is completely rotation-spin entangled, meaning that it does not admit any separable states. Second, we identify isomers whose position states house an internal pseudo-spin or "fiber" degree of freedom, and the fiber's Berry phase or matrix after adiabatic changes in position yields naturally robust operations, akin to braiding anyonic quasiparticles or realizing fault-tolerant quantum gates. We outline how the fiber can be used as a quantum error-correcting code and discuss scenarios where these features can be experimentally probed
item.dc:creator: Victor V. Albert, Eric Kubischta, Mikhail Lemeshko, Lee R. Liu

item.title: Spin-resolved microscopy of $^{87}$Sr SU($N$) Fermi-Hubbard systems
item.description: arXiv:2603.05478v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Quantum-gas microscopes provide direct access to the phases of the Hubbard model, bringing microscopic insight into the complex competition between interactions, SU(2) magnetism, and doping. Alkaline-earth(-like) fermions extend this spin-1/2 paradigm by realizing higher symmetries and giving access to SU($N$) Hubbard models, with rich phase diagrams to be unveiled. Despite its fundamental interest, a microscopic exploration of SU($N$) quantum systems has remained elusive. Here we report the realization of a quantum-gas microscope for fermionic $^{87}$Sr. Our imaging scheme, based on cooling and fluorescence on the narrow intercombination line at 689 nm, enables spin-resolved single-atom detection. By implementing a spin-selective optical pumping protocol, we determine the occupation of each of the 10 spin states in a single experimental realization, a crucial capability for probing site-resolved magnetic correlations. We benchmark our method by observing single-particle Larmor precession across the full spin-9/2 ground-state manifold and use numerical simulations of SU($N$) Fermi-Hubbard chains, incorporating the measured detection fidelities, to demonstrate its capability to resolve many-body spin correlations. Our results establish $^{87}$Sr quantum-gas microscopy as a powerful approach to study exotic magnetism in the SU($N$) Fermi-Hubbard model, and provide a new detection tool for studies in quantum simulation, computation, and metrology.
item.dc:creator: Carlos Gas-Ferrer, Antonio Rubio-Abadal, Sandra Buob, Leonardo Bezzo, Jonatan H\"oschele, Leticia Tarruell
